update_from: API rates: OpenAI 'Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol' post (2026-06-26), re-confirmed against the OpenAI model-pricing table captured 2026-07-10 (GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna default-tier rates match exactly; that table also lists GPT-5.3-Codex at $1.75/$0.175/$14.00 and long-context threshold tiers not yet modeled here). Re-check https://platform.openai.com/docs/pricing once GA. Plan prices: https://openai.com/chatgpt/pricing. GA re-confirmed 2026-07-18 against the announcement + API pricing table (Sol/Terra/Luna default rates match this file exactly; long-context step-up tiers now published — recorded in long_context_note, deliberately not yet modeled).
model_ids_note: UNCONFIRMED ids: the article names capability tiers (Sol/Terra/Luna), not id strings. These ids follow the lowercase-dot-version convention precedented by the doc-confirmed gpt-5.3-codex id on the Copilot side. Confirm against Codex CLI's /model picker (or ~/.codex/config.toml / rollout turn_context records) and correct them HERE (only here) if the CLI disagrees. Roster minimal by design: only GPT-5.6 rates are authoritative from the article; add other Codex-selectable models only with captured authoritative rates. Exception: 'codex-auto-review' is a non-selectable, non-routing observed id (Codex Desktop's auto-review feature) whose backing model the rollouts do not expose; its rate is an ASSUMED best-effort equal to GPT-5.3-Codex — clearly labeled, not authoritative — correct or remove if the true rate surfaces.

api.note: Token-metered API pricing (OPENAI_API_KEY auth). The per-model rates below are authoritative for this mode.

subscription.note: Codex CLI under a ChatGPT plan (ChatGPT sign-in) draws down opaque usage/rate limits, not dollars. OpenAI publishes no token-to-quota conversion: any dollar figure shown for a subscription run is an API-equivalent relative-burn proxy and must be labeled as such — never presented as a bill. GPT-5.6 is GA across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API (announcement, 2026-07-18 capture); plan-level limits remain unpublished — never fabricate an allowance.

cache_note: GPT-5.6 and later: explicit cache breakpoints with a 30-minute minimum cache life. Cache writes bill at 1.25x the uncached input rate; cache reads get the 90% cached-input discount (0.1x). Cached rates are computed from these multipliers at run time — never stored per model.
long_context_note: Authoritative long-context step-up rates (GA API pricing table, captured 2026-07-18), NOT modeled in this file's schema — the codex estimator prices default-tier rates only, and threshold-tier modeling is a separate kit's concern. Single correctable point: GPT-5.6 Sol >272K input → $10.00/$1.00/$45.00; Terra >272K → $5.00/$0.50/$22.50; Luna >200K → $2.00/$0.20/$9.00 (input/cached-input/output per 1M tokens).

plus.note: Usage-limited; no published token allowance exists — never fabricate one.

pro.note: Higher limits than Plus; still no published token allowance.

knobs.reasoning_efforts_note: Ascending API tokens (GPT-5.6 announcement, 2026-07-18 capture). 'max' is the new deepest level with GPT-5.6 — it gives even more reasoning time than 'xhigh' — and may need to be toggled on in settings in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Effort is set per model.

ultra.note: New with GPT-5.6: coordinates four agents in parallel by default to accelerate complex work (the API's multi-agent beta). A MODE, not a rung on the reasoning-effort ladder. CLI surface and pricing unpublished as of the 2026-07-18 capture — no flag or multiplier invented.

fast.note: Codex fast mode: priority processing for time-sensitive work — the published speed lever. CLI surface and pricing impact unpublished as of cached_date — no flag or multiplier invented.

gpt-5.6-sol.notes: Flagship / most capable durable tier. Reach for it deliberately: long-horizon agentic runs, hard architecture/debugging, work a mid-tier model failed on. Also launching on Cerebras at up to 750 tokens/sec (a speed fact, not a price).

gpt-5.6-terra.notes: Balanced everyday tier — competitive with GPT-5.5 at 2x cheaper. The default workhorse: day-to-day coding, tests, docs, refactors.

gpt-5.6-luna.notes: Fast & affordable tier, lowest cost: classification, extraction, formatting, lookups, bulk — and the cheap speed lever.

codex-auto-review.notes: Codex Desktop's automatic code-review feature (rollout originator 'Codex Desktop'), observed in ~/.codex logs. Opaque id: rollouts expose no backing model, so it is NOT user-selectable and NOT a routing target — tier 'non-routing' is outside the cheap|mid|strong|frontier vocabulary and is skipped by resolve_tier. Rates are an ASSUMED best-effort equal to GPT-5.3-Codex (doc-confirmed $1.75/$0.175/$14.00 per the 2026-07-10 OpenAI pricing table) so the daily journal can price it as a labeled API-equivalent proxy — never authoritative; correct or remove if the true backing model/rate is confirmed.

tier_note: Tier vocabulary is shared across all three harnesses (cheap|mid|strong|frontier). OpenAI ships three durable tiers, so 'strong' is unpopulated on this roster: tier resolution takes the first model in file order carrying the tier, skipping upward past empty tiers (strong resolves to the frontier model today). The 'codex-auto-review' entry carries tier 'non-routing' (outside the vocabulary) so resolve_tier never selects it — it exists only so the journal can price an observed, non-selectable id.
